location: Boundaries > Always > Runner (run's own stop: 'every other admitted cell without a record this run (tracked per cell) gets `stopped`')
issue: The sweep has no stated exceptions, but some admitted cells legitimately have no record by the time the stop is handled. (a) A child reaped earlier in the run that exited 2 or reported `skipped`: the first Runner sentence allows zero records for these cells. (b) A cell whose real record failed to append (append error): the run then attempts `stopped` with `force=True`. (c) A done-but-unreaped child that exited 2 or reported `skipped` at stop time. Read literally, 'every other admitted cell without a record' writes `stopped` for all three. That gives an exit-2 or skipped version an inconclusive record, and gives a finished cell a `stopped` record in place of its lost real one. It is unclear whether 'other' means 'cells of children not done when the stop is handled' or 'any admitted cell lacking a record'.
implementation_impact: The stop path either writes `stopped` for exit-2, skipped and append-failed cells or leaves them alone. The two readings produce different histories, different `reached` values and different `blocked-infra` counts. The new run-stop test cannot pin it down either way.
suggestion: Scope the sweep explicitly. `stopped` goes only to admitted cells whose child was still running, or whose future raised `JobStopped`, when the stop was handled. A cell of a child already reaped, or done at stop time, keeps whatever the normal reap rules give it, which may be no record (exit 2, skipped, append error).

location: Boundaries > Always > Runner ('A stop never lands between a record's write and its bookkeeping: it is deferred around each append') and Tasks > tests ('a stop injected mid-append leaves exactly one record for that cell')
issue: The spec says what must not be used (a main-thread `pthread_sigmask` alone) but not what the deferral is. The choices are: swap `_on_sigterm` for a flag-setting handler around the critical section and re-raise `JobStopped` afterwards, or block the signal process-wide. The deferral also covers only a single append, so a stop can still land mid-`_on_reaped`: the future is already popped from `self.running` and some of that child's cells are already appended. It can also land mid-`_fire`, after some queued versions already got `not-run` and their logs were truncated to `DONE rc=not-run`. Separately, the test cannot be written by raising `JobStopped` from a patched `append_record`: an exception raised synchronously goes around any signal-based deferral. The test has to deliver a real SIGTERM with the `job_register` handler installed, and the spec does not say so.
implementation_impact: Two implementers would build different deferral mechanisms. A stop that lands mid-reap can leave a done child half-recorded, with the rest of its cells swept into `stopped` instead of getting their real results. The mid-append test may pass while proving nothing.
suggestion: Name the mechanism: while `_append` and the per-child bookkeeping in `_on_reaped`/`_fire` run, the SIGTERM handler only sets a flag, and `JobStopped` is raised when the section exits. Extend the deferral to the whole reap of one child. Specify the test injection: `os.kill(os.getpid(), SIGTERM)` from inside a patched `append_record`, with the real handler installed.

location: Code Map > ps-plan-layers.py ('new step derivation (pure: configured cells, canary, per-cell records, fingerprint, tags, session, current notes in; step and tier fields out)')
issue: The listed inputs leave out each cell's `corrupt_tail` flag from `read_history`. `has_passing_evidence(records, corrupt_tail, …)` needs it, and the contract (Evidence record > Storage) says a cell with a corrupt tail has no passing gate-grade evidence. The listed inputs also leave out the run scope (`--versions`/`--browsers`), yet `blocked-by-scope`, `e2e_next_cells` vs `e2e_required_cells` and the `out-of-scope` causes depend on it. It is also unstated whether the pure function returns the step before or after the scope filter.
implementation_impact: A derivation that follows this signature literally calls `has_passing_evidence(..., False, ...)`. A corrupt-tail cell whose older valid records pass would then count as passing: `done`, or `gate` from a canary with a corrupt tail. That breaks the honesty law. Unit tests built on the listed signature cannot express scope cases.
suggestion: Add `corrupt_tail` per cell and the scope (versions, browsers) to the pure function's inputs. State that it returns both the unfiltered step and the filtered result (the `blocked-by-scope` rewrite included). Add a unit case: a corrupt tail after a passing canary derives `focus` or `cold-canary`, not `gate`.

location: Boundaries > Always > Docs (Headless: 'stop at the first unclean step, `reached`/`not reached`, `e2e_tier_reached`') and cell-contract.md > Headless
issue: A headless step is 'clean when every cell in its `e2e_next_cells` has passing gate-grade evidence or is not-gradeable after the run'. Neither the spec nor the contract says how the orchestrator judges that without reading histories. One option is a post-run plan call (the cells absent from the e2e `rerun_matrix`, or carrying reason `not-gradeable`). Another is the run's exit code. `e2e_tier_reached` is '{tier, step} from the last plan call', and `not reached: stopped at <step>` names a step. After a failed canary or gate run, the last plan call is the post-run one, which already shows the next step (for example `focus` after a gate failure). So the step that failed and the step reported can differ.
implementation_impact: The headless return can report a step the run never attempted, and the four callers would log a misleading stop point. Two doc writers would pick different cleanliness checks.
suggestion: Specify it: after each E2E run, headless makes one plan call (same flags). The step was clean iff none of the run's `e2e_next_cells` has an e2e `rerun_matrix` entry other than reason `not-gradeable`. `e2e_tier_reached` and `stopped at <step>` use the step and tier of the plan call that chose the run, not the post-run call.

location: Boundaries > Always > Docs (4th interim rule: 'A run left an infra cause when the next plan's e2e `rerun_matrix` reason for a cell in its `appended` is … and that cell's record from the run is not `stopped` (the run exited 143, or its stderr reports the child stopped)')
issue: A run that exits 143 prints no output line (ps-run-layer docstring, existing stop test: `out.strip() == ''`). It therefore has no `appended`. The parenthetical '(the run exited 143 …)' describes a case where the `appended` test can never apply. So after an interactive exit 143 that Budi chooses to rerun, done children with real infra causes (for example `crash`) are never detected, and the environment-fix prompt is skipped. The rule also does not say which stderr line counts as 'reports the child stopped'. Today it is `versi <ver>: anak dihentikan (rc=…)`, per version rather than per cell.
implementation_impact: The doc writer has to invent how the exit-143 case is detected, or drop it. The interactive orchestrator may rerun straight into the same infra failure without the decided prompt.
suggestion: Either state that after exit 143 no infra check applies (the rerun is Budi's explicit request), or have the orchestrator take the cells from the command's `--cells` when there is no output line. Quote the exact stderr marker (per version) that excludes a version's cells.

location: Boundaries > Always > Docs (Headless: 'config copy with canary reset, only for a well-formed canary outside the set, a malformed one kept') and AC 3
issue: 'Well-formed' is not defined, and the model applies the rule by judgment because no script writes the copy. The normalizer rules are: a string, trimmed, exactly one `:`, parts trimmed, browser lower-cased, version compared as an exact string, no engine or version-format check. Under these rules it is unclear whether `9.1:safari`, `x.y:chromium`, `9.1:Chromium ` or a list value is 'well-formed but outside the set' (reset, run continues) or 'malformed' (kept, plan exit 2, headless `blocked`).
implementation_impact: The same config gives `complete` or `blocked` depending on how the doc writer, and later the model at runtime, reads 'well-formed'. AC 3 only covers the clear case.
suggestion: Define 'well-formed' in the docs in normalizer terms. Proposed: a string that, after trimming, splits at exactly one `:` into two non-empty trimmed parts. Everything else is malformed. State that the browser-part case and engine support do not matter for the reset.

location: Boundaries > Always > Docs (Headless) vs cell-contract.md > Headless bullet 3; spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md > Never ('new return fields' deferred)
issue: CAP-2 deferred 'the new return fields' to this slice. The contract's headless return gains `versions: {<ver>: {e2e_state, reason}}` and `not_run_cells`, both copied from the aggregate run with `--session`. `headless.md` today returns neither. The spec's Headless list names `reached`/`not reached` and `e2e_tier_reached` but not these two fields. Yet the four callers' new 'not reached' handling reads `versions[ver].reason`, which only exists once `versions` is in the return.
implementation_impact: A doc writer following the spec's explicit list could add `e2e_tier_reached` and the 'not reached' wording but no `versions`/`not_run_cells` in the return. The callers' updated SKILL.md would then read a field headless never returns.
suggestion: Add to the Headless list: 'the return gains `versions` (per-version `e2e_state`, `reason`) and `not_run_cells`, copied from the aggregate run with this call's `--session`'. Have Verification > Manual check that `headless.md` > Kembalian lists them.

location: Design Notes > `clean` ('one that does not load, fails `validate_layer_shape` (static, flashlight) or is a scenario payload whose `versions` is not an object = exit 2')
issue: The note does not say which `finding_keys` the static gate uses. ps-aggregate uses `("id", "severity", "message")` because `static_layer` indexes `f["id"]` directly. With `()` a static finding missing `id` passes the gate and crashes `static_layer` (KeyError → traceback, exit 1). The scenario gate checks only the top-level `versions` type. `scenario_layer` also calls `.get` on `versions[V]` and on each `scenarios[i]`, so a non-object entry crashes it too.
implementation_impact: A malformed per-version file whose `phase1_reuse` is true can crash the plan with exit 1, a code orchestrator docs never handle, instead of the specified exit 2 naming the file.
suggestion: State: static is gated with ps-aggregate's keys `(id, severity, message)`, flashlight with `()`. For scenario, `versions` must be an object, `versions[V]` an object, and `scenarios`, if present, a list of objects. Any violation = exit 2 naming the file.

location: Boundaries > Always > Docs (hosting loop and Phase 2 loop) vs cell-contract.md > Plan step 5 and Run scope
issue: A `cold-version` step lists every configured browser of V whatever its evidence. If the run scope excludes some of V's browsers (for example `--browsers chromium` while the focus cell is V:firefox), the filter leaves [V:chromium]. That is not empty, so there is no `blocked-by-scope`. After V:chromium passes, the focus cell and its warm or partial pass are unchanged, so the plan derives the same `cold-version` [V:chromium] again. The hosting loop, which ends only at `gate`/`done`/loop ended, reruns it forever. The step is unreachable in CAP-1 practice (only warm or partial records reach step 5). But the CAP-1 docs and tests (hand-written warm records) define the loop now, and nothing documents the terminal case.
implementation_impact: The docs written now encode an endless hosting loop that surfaces as soon as CAP-4/5 land, or as soon as a test drives the scoped `cold-version` state through more than one iteration.
suggestion: Add an orchestrator rule (or an Ask First note for the contract): a step whose filtered `e2e_next_cells` all already hold fresh passing gate-grade evidence while the step is unchanged is treated as `blocked-by-scope` and ends the E2E loop. At minimum, record it as a known CAP-4/5 follow-up.

location: Tasks > tests (run-stop test: '`--slots 3` and four versions (one reaped, one done but unreaped holding a `fail`, one still running, one queued …)')
issue: The fixture is under-specified and, as written, internally inconsistent. (a) The 'one reaped' child's outcome is not given. If it is a `fail`, or exits 2, `_fire` writes `not-run` for the queued version, which contradicts 'nothing for the queued one'. (b) After the first child is reaped, its claim is released, so 2 running + 1 ≤ 3 and the next pass admits the fourth version, unless the stubbed `daemon_slot_usage` is raised after that reap. (c) The existing `test_e2e_stopped` (`JobStopped` from the 9.1 future's `result()`, expecting `_hist(9.1) == []` and no output line) must also change: under the new rule that cell gets `stopped`. The Tasks mention only the single-child SIGTERM case.
implementation_impact: The test writer has to guess the fixture. A naive harness either admits the 'queued' version or fires fail-fast, and the test fails for reasons unrelated to the stop path. The old stop test silently contradicts the new rule.
suggestion: Specify it. The reaped child passes. The stubbed daemon count rises to fill the cap once that child is reaped, so the fourth version stays queued. Also list `test_e2e_stopped`'s `JobStopped` sub-case: the 9.1 cell now gets one `stopped` record, still no output line, exit 143.

location: Boundaries > Always > Runner ('`--tier 0|1` … stamped as `tier` on every record')
issue: The record type is not stated. The CLI value is a string. The plan's `e2e_tier` is an integer (or null), and the contract says `tier` = 'the plan's `e2e_tier`'.
implementation_impact: The runner may write `"tier": "0"`, so later readers (CAP-6 timing reports, tests comparing `tier == 0`) diverge.
suggestion: State: `tier` is written as the integer 0 or 1. argparse uses `type=int, choices=(0, 1)`, or equivalent validation keeps the exit 2 for any other value.

location: Tasks > tests vs cell-contract.md > State, freshness, gate-grade ('Test: pass then fail on the same fingerprint gives `ready=false` and a step other than `done`')
issue: CAP-2 implemented this contract test without the step ('no step'), because steps were out of scope. CAP-1 owns `e2e_step`, but neither its Tasks nor its I/O matrix adds the 'step other than `done`' assertion. The contract's step 5/6 test ('pass then fail does not promote') is covered by Promote order only for warm passes, not for two cold full records.
implementation_impact: A derivation bug that picks the older gate-grade pass (for example `done` with a newer cold fail) would pass every listed test.
suggestion: Add to Tasks > tests: a cold full pass then a cold full fail on the current fingerprint for one cell derives a step other than `done` (`focus` on that cell), and the aggregate `ready` is false.

location: Boundaries > Always > Runner ('a child reaped with `STOPPED_CODES` … even one whose engine finished before the signal') vs Docs (4th interim rule) and the `appended` output
issue: Single-child stops now append `stopped` records, so their cells appear in the output line's `appended`. Since `stopped` maps to plan reason `inconclusive`, the 4th rule needs the stderr marker to exclude them. The marker `versi <ver>: anak dihentikan` is per version, and the spec does not say whether ps-run-layer's log text changes, even though the existing log says 'tak ada rekaman untuk versi ini' (no record for this version). That message becomes false.
implementation_impact: The runner keeps a log line that contradicts its new behaviour, and the docs' infra-cause exclusion depends on log wording the spec never pins.
suggestion: Require the STOPPED_CODES log line to read, for example, `versi <ver>: anak dihentikan (rc=…) — sel <cells> dicatat stopped`. Have the docs quote that marker for the 4th rule.

location: Never ('the bankwire timing report') vs SPEC.md > Success signal
issue: SPEC.md makes the before/after bankwire timing report mandatory. 'Before' must run 'on the scripts of the commit preceding the first script change', and that commit predates CAP-2, which is already merged. The spec lists the report under 'later slices' but names no slice that owns it. CAP-1 is the slice whose tier ordering produces the 'after' release-gate measurement (cold canary run plus tier-1 run).
implementation_impact: Nobody is tasked with the report. The baseline commit keeps getting further away and may stop working on the current host. Each later slice can defer it again.
suggestion: Name the owning slice (for example the one that lands CAP-5/CAP-7) and the baseline commit hash for 'before' (the parent of CAP-2's first script change), so the deferral is traceable.

issue: `CONFIG_KEY_TO_DEST` is listed, but no task says what changes in it. The contract says the canary has no flag and is read directly from `--config`. Adding `psm_e2e_canary` there would make `apply_config_file` fill a dest on any script that has one. The plan's new `--browsers` is filled from the existing `psm_e2e_browsers → browsers` mapping with no edit. The `configured_cells` docstring also says 'psm_e2e_canary diabaikan slice ini' (psm_e2e_canary is ignored this slice), and the spec does not say whether the canary is folded into `configured_cells`. Folding it in would make ps-run-layer's `--merge-only` (which calls `configured_cells`) reject a bad canary, against 'non-`--merge-only` runs only'.
implementation_impact: The implementer may edit the key map without need, or fold canary parsing into `configured_cells` and so break `--merge-only` on a bad canary.
suggestion: State: `CONFIG_KEY_TO_DEST` stays unchanged (listed only because the plan's `--browsers` relies on it). The canary normalizer is a separate function that plan, aggregate and `read_e2e_config` call explicitly. `configured_cells` keeps its signature and drops the 'ignored this slice' note.
